question: Recently, at the Berlin International Film Festival, anti-Semitic statements were made on stage and applauded by some of those present1. Meanwhile, AfD politicians, who had not done anything wrong, were disinvited solely on the basis of their party affiliation2. In light of these events, the political neutrality and the values that should be reflected in EU-funded events are being called into question.
This situation raises concerns about how consistently the requirement for political neutrality is being applied, in particular with regard to spending taxpayers’ money. 1.

How does the Commission view the fact that the festival organisers chose to exclude specific political groups, while at the same time statements that could be perceived as anti-Semitic were tolerated at the event?
Is this at odds with the political neutrality that should be ensured when using EU funds?

Will the Commission consider making future funding conditional on political neutrality and does the Commission plan to audit the funding already paid to the Berlin International Film Festival in order to verify compliance with these principles?
answer: The Commission is committed to fight antisemitism, as stated in its EU Strategy on combating antisemitism and fostering Jewish life (3) and has reiterated its engagement against hatred in its communication No place for hate: a Europe united against hatred (4). The Berlinale Film Festival is an independent organisation.
While it receives support from the Creative Europe MEDIA programme (5), the Commission cannot interfere with the internal governance and decision-making process of its beneficiaries.

The Commission implements the Creative Europe MEDIA programme in accordance with Regulation (EU) 2021/818 (6) which adheres to the values laid out in Article 2 of the Treaty on European Union (TEU), including freedom of expression and artistic freedom. The Commission monitors the implementation of all its projects.

The interim evaluation of the Creative Europe MEDIA programme is ongoing and will be finalised by 31 December 2024. The Commission recalls that the next multiannual financial framework (MFF) proposal and the related outcome of the negotiations cannot be prejudged at this stage. The Commission will table a proposal for a new MFF by 1 July 2025.
